dossier.public_summary: The 1.01-day dip on this M dwarf coincides exactly with the star's strong 1.01-day spot modulation, which is much larger (6547 ppm) than the dip itself. Difference imaging puts the signal on the target with no nearby star that could mimic it, so it is stellar variability aliased as a transit, not a planet.

reasons.why: A very large out-of-eclipse swing, larger than the 4920 ppm dip itself, is the hallmark of stellar variability / a close binary, not a planet transit.
The dip period is exactly the star's spot period (to 1 part in 10^7) with enormous 20000+ ppm modulation, i.e. the signal is the variability itself, not a planet at that period.
